A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JME research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Gaussian density-estimation simulations and CIFAR-10 training experiments, with numerical training results in Appendix B.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the original simulations and CIFAR-10 experiments and report an additional Gaussian density-estimation configuration.

M1.justification: JME, lambda-JME, and JME-Adam retain their perturbation procedures, sensitivity-based scaling, and diagonal second-moment adaptation. The mathematical corrections do not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 3(b) adds ten-dimensional Gaussian streams alongside the earlier five-dimensional density-estimation example. This modestly expands synthetic input-dimensionality coverage; CIFAR-10 and the two application tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged, but IME's specified calibration in Algorithm 4 changes: v1 separately calibrates linearly split epsilon/delta budgets, whereas v2 uses sigma/sqrt(alpha) and sigma/sqrt(1-alpha). IME remains in Figure 1; the PDFs do not establish that its plotted results were recomputed.

E3.justification: The added Gaussian configuration specifies d=10, n=200, and sigma=4, alongside the retained d=5, sigma=2 case. CIFAR-10 budgets, batch sizes, training duration, and hyperparameters are unchanged. The clarified noise notation does not itself establish rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: The existing debiasing comparisons and dimensionality, workload, and factorization analyses are retained, including figures moved into Appendix B. The additional Gaussian configuration extends benchmark evaluation without introducing a distinct ablation or robustness-analysis question.

E5.justification: Both versions report Gaussian simulation means and standard deviations over 1000 runs and CIFAR-10 means and standard deviations over three runs. The additional Gaussian panel follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 3(b) adds KL-divergence curves showing JME's advantage over PP in the d=10, sigma=4 configuration. All 80 CIFAR-10 mean/standard-deviation entries match between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2. The added curves are new-setting results, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 corrects second-moment error scaling from zeta to zeta squared; Lemma 3.8 and Corollary 3.9 revise related scaling factors. The proof of Theorem A.2 corrects the optimized expression from -beta-2lambda beta squared to -2beta-2lambda beta squared. These are localized corrections rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract now qualifies second-moment estimation's lack of additional privacy cost as occurring in an identified privacy regime. The introduction and conclusion retain the same joint-estimation contribution and claims of advantages in high-privacy regimes.

C2.justification: A new footnote to Lemma 3.5 explains why decreasing column norms are assumed, how numerical maximization over column indices can relax that restriction, and why the intended Toeplitz matrices satisfy it. Existing performance interpretations and open questions remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 4 revises the explicit instructions for reproducing IME's noise calibration. v2 also clarifies the relationship between the Gaussian multiplier and actual first-moment noise. The CIFAR-10 hyperparameter table is unchanged, and no new hardware or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds discussion and citations on precise sensitivity analysis, including Lebeda, Joseph et al., and Wilkins et al., and recent matrix-factorization research. This modestly expands positioning while retaining the earlier covariance-estimation and DP-Adam context.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording corrections, changes several subsection headings to run-in headings, adopts numbered citations, and places the algorithms appendix before the technical proofs. Most prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive reflow of equations and displays. The workload table and two analytical figures move to Appendix B, v1's methods-overview Table 2 is removed, and the Gaussian experimental figure gains a second panel.

improvement.justification: Corrected error scaling and proof algebra, clearer noise conventions, and IME calibration consistent with the Gaussian-composition argument improve internal consistency. The additional Gaussian case provides modest corroboration. Removing the useful methods-overview table reduces convenience, but the corrections support a limited net improvement rather than a substantial change in scientific quality.
